topic: Why A Pencil Looks Broken In Water
creativeBrief:
Pattern: CONTRADICTION_REVEAL_V4. Five voiced scenes of 6s each: contradiction, clue, clue, mechanism, second_reveal/payoff. Target 25-29s. Visible change every 2-3s. Reveal in scene 4. Scene 5 ends on the same framing as scene 1 so it loops. Use lockedVoiceover word for word.
YouTube title seed: Why Does This Pencil Look Broken?
YouTube description seed: It's one straight pencil. So why does it look snapped? #TellMeWhyyyyyy #Shorts
The central fact: Light slows down in water and changes direction at the boundary between water and air.
The later surprise: The same effect makes a fish appear to be where it isn't, so spearfishers miss.
The very first frame: A yellow pencil standing in a clear glass of water on a plain white background, visibly snapped at the waterline, filling most of the frame. No hand, no pouring, no text. Nothing in the first second gives the answer away.
Hook test: A (statement) = "This pencil isn't broken."; B (question) = "Why does this pencil look broken?".
Animation prompts (low motion, camera moves only, nothing passes through objects, no text):
Scene 1: Locked-off camera, very slow push-in on the pencil in the glass; pencil and water stay still.
Scene 2: Slow lateral camera slide around the glass at the waterline; the pencil stays still.
Scene 3: Slow camera tilt down from the waterline to the bottom half of the pencil underwater.
Scene 4: Slow camera orbit around the glass, side view at the waterline; pencil and water still.
Scene 5: Slow pull-back from a calm clear pond with a still fish, ending on the scene 1 framing of the pencil in the glass.
Fact boundaries: Lines 1-3 do not mention light, bending, refraction or water. The main reveal lands in scene 4.

facts.statement: When light travels from air into water it slows down, causing it to change direction at the boundary.
The eye and brain assume light travels in a straight line, so the underwater part of the pencil appears to be somewhere it isn't and the straight pencil appears broken.
Because light refracts between water and air, a fish appears to be at a location where it isn't, so a spearfishing hunter aiming at it misses.

factBoundaries: The pencil itself is straight and unbroken.
Only refraction at the water-air boundary; do not claim magnification or other effects.
